chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Hamdan al-Qalanisi from Ishaq ibn Bunan from Ibn Baqqah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A woman claimed against her husband, in the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), that he does not copulate with her, and he claimed that he does copulate with her. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered her to apply saffron to herself, then he should wash his penis. If the water came out yellow, he was believed; otherwise, he was ordered to divorce her.

key_terms.صَدَّقَهُ: He was believed / his claim was verified
key_terms.يُجَامِعُهَا: He copulates with her / consummates the marriage

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (AS) resolve disputes over sexual consummation in early Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and empirical evidence in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) utilizes saffron as a natural indicator to resolve a *khilaf* (dispute) between spouses regarding consummation. The procedure highlights the legal principle that if the wife claims non-consummation and the husband denies it, the burden of proof shifts, and the physical test serves as a decisive *qarinah* (sign) to either validate the husband's claim or trigger the obligation of divorce (*talaq*) to prevent ongoing uncertainty. This method reflects the early caliphal judicial practices attributed to Imam Ali (AS) and underscores the Shia emphasis on accessible, tangible proofs in family law.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Hamdan Al qalanasy, from Is’haq Bin Bunan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A woman claimed upon her husband, in the era of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> that he does not copulate with her, but he denied it. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> ordered her that she should apply herself with saffron, then he should wash his manhood, so if the water comes to be yellow, he would be ratified, or else he<sup>asws</sup> ordered with divorcing her’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Hamdan al-Qalanisiy from Ishaq ibn Bunan from ibn Baqqah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that during the time of ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, a woman alleged that her husband is not able to go to bed with her and he denied it. ’Amir al- Mu’minin commanded her to fill up herself with saffron and that he then washes his penis; if the water takes the color of saffron his words are accepted, otherwise, he is commanded to divorce her.’”
